item.title: The Busy Mom Webinar: Social Security Basics — Wed Aug 12, 12:00 AM
item.description: Join Mary Jo Kerrigan, Financial Advisor at Equitable Advisors, on the second Wednesday of each month for a brief, informative webinar designed to help you make smarter financial decisions with confidence. Designed with busy moms who don't have time to waste in mind, each session delivers practical insights you can put to work right away - all in just 20 minutes. Social Security is an important source of retirement income. But knowing when and how to claim your benefits can have a lasting impact on your financial future. During this session, we'll cover the basics of Social Security, including: How your benefits are calculated When you can begin claiming benefits How claiming age affects your monthly benefit Key factors to consider before making your decision Common mistakes to avoid Whether retirement is just around the corner or still a few years away, this session will provide the foundational knowledge you need to make more informed decisions about your retirement income. item.title: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again - Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM
item.description: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone. item.title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg — Sat Aug 22, 1:00 PM
item.description: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. No artistic experience required. No right or wrong. Just a fresh set of eyes and a willingness to see the overlooked as raw material for something new. Unrec

item.title: Library Speakers Consortium - Writing the Nightmare: A Ship Called Sickness and One Unforgettable Space Crew with Daniel Kraus — Tue Sep 8, 7:00 PM — Nutley Free Public Library
item.description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/194581
Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik.
Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as “niks,” has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fém—a plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue.
The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, and—most lethal of all—a rugged, NonModded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter.

item.title: Shawangunks Loop Hike — Sun Aug 23, 9:00 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this interesting loop hike in the Shawangunks of New York! For this 15 mile loop trip, we will meet at the Foordmore Trailhead for the Long Path near Kerkhonksen New York. The most difficult parts will be the very beginning where we ascend the Shawangunk Ridge on backroads and the Stony Kill Carriageway. Once we reach the top of the ridge, we continue a bit through the blueberry lands, and then descend a bit on Smiley Carriageway. There will be one rough bit of trail down to a waterfall, and then more pleasant back roads. There is one bit that has metal rungs to climb up, but it is quite short. I'll be prepared with a pack to carry all of Ev's stuff for this stretch. The only regular road walk stuff is pretty much at the very beginning, and the beginning of the ascent. item.title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles — Sat Aug 29, 4:00 PM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **Saturday, August 29 4-7pm**
Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation.
Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs. Sponsered by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association.
Meet at Clipper Pavilion (Not by McLoone's) on Cherry Lane in West Orange.
[Advance registration required via rahwayriver.org/calendar.html ](https://rahwayriver.org/calendar.html)Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.
Leader: Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway River Watershed Association (RRWA) and expert on local watershed issues.
Meet at: The gazebo by the dog park along Crest Drive in Maplewood.

item.title: Brandywine Hike — Sun Aug 30, 9:00 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point 15 mile hike, the next in the Brandywine Series! This time, we'll travel between Delacy Soccer Complex in East Bradford Township and Downingtown. We already covered some of Downingtown previously, but this time we'll cover some other municipal trails and former route of the Brandywine Trail near the beginning, as well as the end of Struble Trail, Lions Trail, and we'll trace the historic route of the Pennsylvania Railroad New Holland Branch briefly. From here, we take some new creekside trails, and then make our way on the Brandywine Trail up to the Philadelphia and Thorndale Branch. We take another municipal trail from here south to a pleasant back road with no lines in it, and then revisit the Harmony Hill Covered Bridge.
